questions.q: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.
o: are grandest than
The Dussehra celebrations
any other part
questions.s:
Correct Answer: are grandest than

Solution:
The phrase "are grandest than" is grammatically incorrect. The word "grandest" is the superlative form and should be used with "the", not with "than".
When making a comparison between two or more things, we use the comparative form (grander) with "than", not the superlative.

Correct form: "are grander than"

✅ Correct sentence: The Dussehra celebrations in Mysore this year are grander than in any other part of the state.

Meanings:
grandest – the most magnificent – सबसे भव्य
grander – more magnificent (comparison) – अधिक भव्य
celebrations – events to mark an occasion – उत्सव
state – a region within a country – राज्य

questions.q: After coming from a long journey he said, "It feels so_______to be home".
questions.s:
After a linking verb like feel, we use an adjective, not a comparative degree unless a comparison exists.
It feels so good to be home.

questions.q: This book is (a) / the most best (b) / in the series. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: The error is in part (b). 'Best' is a superlative adjective, so 'most' is incorrect. Correct form is 'the best.' Answer: (b). 'Best' superlative hai, isliye 'most' galat hai. Sahi form hai 'the best.' Jawab: (b).

questions.q: This painting is as beautiful as, if not more then, the one in the museum.
o: This painting is as beautiful as
the one in the museum.
questions.s:
The correct option is: (b) if not more then

The phrase "if not more than" is used to introduce a possibility that the quality being compared might exceed the quality of the standard being used. In this case, it suggests that the painting being discussed may be even more beautiful than the one in the museum.

So, the corrected sentence would be: "This painting is as beautiful as, if not more than, the one in the museum."

questions.q:
Solar storms can / impact Earth-dwellers / in significantly ways.

[MTS-06/07/2022 S1]
questions.s: The adverb "significantly" should modify the adjective "ways," but it is not properly positioned. The correct adjective here"in significant ways".

questions.q: The people of ancient India (a)/ were more civilized (b)/ than ancient Europe. (c)/ No error (d)
questions.s: Use "than those of ancient Europe" or "than the people of ancient Europe.”

questions.q: He found (a wooden broken chair) in the room,
questions.s:
Adjective order rule: Opinion → Size → Age → Shape → Colour → Origin → Material → Purpose + Noun
Condition comes before material, so the correct order is: a broken wooden chair

questions.q: (a) Krishna ran to the /(b) nearing grocery store to /(c) buy biscuits as his parents were expecting guests. /(d) No error

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The mango is the ______ fruit.
questions.s:
The sentence implies a superlative quality of the mango compared to other fruits. The superlative form of the adjective "sweet" is "sweetest," indicating the mango is the most sweet among all fruits. "Sweetly" is an adverb, "sweet" is the base adjective, and "sweeter" is comparative, none of which fit the superlative context.

Thus, "sweetest" is the correct choice.

The complete sentence is: "The mango is the sweetest fruit."

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement required.

I had never travelled abroad prior than last year's trip to Japan.
questions.s:
The following are used as comparative adjectives and are followed by to and not 'than': superior, senior, junior, inferior, prior, anterior, posterior, prefer, etc.

The correct sentence is- I had never travelled abroad prior to last year's trip to Japan.

Hence, option (c) is correct.

questions.q: They bought a sturdy, medium, brown, rectangular, Canadian, wooden desk for the home office.
o: They bought a sturdy, medium
wooden desk for the home office.
questions.s:
If the adjective of size, color, age etc. Come together in a sentence, they should be used in this order: Opinion -> Size -> Age -> Shape -> Color -> Origin -> Material -> Purpose. So, The correct option is: (b), brown, rectangular, Canadian,

The correct sentence would be: "They bought a sturdy, medium, rectangular, brown, Canadian, wooden desk for the home office."

questions.q: (a) He ran so fastly /(b) that he reached /(c) the destination in just two minutes. /(d) No error.
According to a recent study, drinking green tea thrice a week is associated with a longest and healthy life.
questions.s:
Explanation:- ‘Longest’ ki jagah par 'long' ka use kren kyunki jab 'and' conjuntion se do adjectives judte hain toh dono same degree me hone chahiye.

Note:- Agar hum yahan 'longer and healthier' likhte toh aur better meaning aata kyunki hume yahan 'green tea na peene walon' ka comparison 'green tea peene walon' se karna hai, isliye 'longer and hearthier' dono comparative degree me likhna better hai.

questions.q: Fred and George had / bewitched there trunks to fly downstairs/to save the bother of carrying them. (SSC MTS Tier-01 13/06/23)
o: Save the bother of carrying them.
bewitched there trunks to fly downstairs to
questions.s: The possessive pronoun 'their' is needed, not the adverb of place 'there'.

questions.q: The radio data shows / neither evidence for / ongoing jet activity. (SSC MTS Tier-01 11/05/23)
questions.s: 'Neither' is used with 'nor'. Without 'nor', 'no' should be used instead: "no evidence for".

questions.q:
It turned out to be the noisy park party anybody had ever attended.

{ CGL Tier-02 08/08/22}
questions.s: The adjective "noisy" should be placed before the noun "party". Also, the word "anybody" should be in the correct form as "anyone" for better clarity and flow. The sentence structure needs to be modified to use the proper comparative form: "the most noisy" or "the noisiest".

questions.s: Should be "good enough a batsman" or "such a good batsman".

questions.q: India's GDP is (a)/ most likely to grow (b)/ at six percent higher than (c)/ those of the US. (d)/ No error (e)
questions.s: It should be either "grow at six percent, higher than that of the US" or "be six percent higher than that of the US.”

questions.q: Ben Essenburg is widely known / as one of the world's best portrayer / of the Everglades. (SSC MTS Tier-01 15/06/23)
o: as one of the world's best portrayer
questions.s: The phrase "one of the" must be followed by a plural noun. It should be 'portrayers'.

questions.q: The view is (a) / very beautiful (b) / from the hill. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: There is no error. 'Very beautiful' is correct for positive degree. Answer: (d). Sentence mein koi galti nahi, 'very beautiful' positive degree ke liye sahi hai. Jawab: (d).
